title: Canary interlock checkpoints and observation templates (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working collection of interlock checkpoints, observation templates, and escalation heuristics for cross-functional canary + A/B rollouts involving LLM-driven product surface area (generation, reranking, embeddings). The goal is to provide concrete, copy-pasteable signal checks and a rehearsal checklist teams can use to move from small samples to broad exposure while keeping latency/cost/quality within agreed SLOs.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Product owners, SRE/Oncall, Applied ML, Observability, Solutions Eng, and Growth PMs running experiments that touch inference routing or model swaps.
- Applies to: Hybrid rollouts that combine traffic canaries, micro-A/B experiments, and staged capacity changes across Hosted/Dedicated/Private modes.
- Not covered here: billing reconciliation; model training/regression analysis (see linked evals doc).

High-level constraints we assume:
- Instrumentation: request-level traces (request_id), per-token latency breakdown, model-version tag, route/campaign tag, and cost-per-request metric are already emitted to the central telemetry pipeline. If any are missing, STOP and add instrumentation.
- Guardrails: every rollout must have an owner and an oncall contact list, and an explicit abort condition.

Definitions (quick):
- Canary (traffic): small-sample live traffic routed to new variant to validate safety and perform real-signal collection.
- Micro-A/B: controlled experiment with manual or automated allocation and hypothesis; can be run in parallel with canaries if exposure is orthogonal.
- Interlock checkpoint: a synchronous/async approval gate requiring signoff or automatic criteria to be met before proceeding to the next exposure step.

Interlock checkpoints (copy-paste templates)
1) Pre-exposure (Checklist + fast sanity)
- Owner: Experiment lead.
- Must pass: unit/integration tests, internal Canary smoke traffic that exercises edge prompts, synthetic adversarial prompts run through the exact routing path.
- Signals to verify (minimum):
  - Model loaded and healthy: GPU memory stable for 15m under synthetic load (metric: gpu.mem.used).
  - Request trace sanity: 99% of synthetic traces include model-version tag, route tag, and latency spans (trace completeness >= 99%).
  - Cost check: Expected cost per token vs baseline within X% (configurable threshold; default 25%).
- Approval: owner + infra (if infra changes are part of rollout).

2) Canary (live traffic low-volume)
- Allocation: start at 0.5% → 1% → 2% in discrete steps (timing depends on request volume; default wait 60m between steps).
- Observation window: minimum 60 minutes after steady-state.
- Signals (automated checks):
  - Latency: p95 latency per request must not increase > 30% vs baseline or exceed absolute SLO (e.g., 500ms) for more than 1% of requests in window.
  - Error rate: 5xx and model-timeout rate <= baseline + 0.1% absolute.
  - Quality: model-level BLEU/ROUGE not applicable for free text — use surrogate signals: fallback-rate, user-correction-rate, rerank-click-delta. These must be within predeclared thresholds.
  - Cost: per-token cost delta <= +40% (if higher, require product approval).
  - Behavioral drift: Automated classifier (safe/reject) flag rate must not increase more than 2x baseline unless approved.
- Human checks: daily PR review of 50 random samples of canary traffic (owner + applied-ml).
- Escalation: if any automated check fails, auto-rollback to previous stable model and notify oncall, product lead, and legal if safety classifier tripped.

3) Experiment ramp (A/B style extension)
- If canary passes, convert a portion of traffic to a controlled experiment cohort: e.g., cohort segmentation by geography or user power-level.
- Allocation plan: 5%→10%→25% (with 24–72h windows depending on metric variance).
- Hypothesis contract: Must declare primary metric, minimum detectable effect, and acceptance criterion before switching allocation.

Observation templates (text to copy into dashboards / incident comments)
- Canary observation snapshot (to paste into Slack/incident):
  - Period: 2025-07-15 10:00 — 2025-07-15 11:00 UTC
  - Canary allocation: 2% (model v2.1.0)
  - Latency p50/p95/p99: 90ms / 320ms / 890ms (baseline p95 240ms)
  - Error rate (5xx): 0.02% (baseline 0.01%) — action: none yet
  - Cost per 1k tokens: $X.XX (delta +12% vs baseline)
  - Safety classifier flags: 14 / 12k requests (baseline 6 / 12k) — note: flagged prompts concentrated in region APAC; alerting oncall
  - Quick sample: [links to 10 anonymized samples for review — redacted IDs: r-1234, r-1239…]

Instrumentation / Dashboard checklist (must be green before ramp)
- Request-level tracing enabled and exported to tracing system.
- Per-model and per-route breakdown available in console.
- Cost taggable to feature flag/id to attribute experiment.
- Canary cohort metrics auto-collected and compared to baseline with rolling windows.
- Synthetic traffic harness scheduled (nightly) that mimics top-100 prompt shapes.

Escalation playbook (short)
- Tier 1: Automated alarm fires (latency/cost/flag-rate thresholds). Oncall triages, posts initial summary, and flips circuit breaker if degradation is > stop-threshold.
- Tier 2: If rollback is not clean or regression persists, convene crossfunctional incident: product, SRE, Applied ML, legal (if safety flags). Collect red-team samples, check model inputs, and run hotfix plan.
- Tier 3: If customer-facing impact is material (customer SLA breach), engage customer success and schedule postmortem immediately with a 48h remediation target.

Canary rollout tempo guidance (heuristic)
- Small teams / low-traffic: longer windows (24–72h) per step; assemble 5–10 human samples per step.
- High-volume features: shorter windows (1–4h) with stricter automated thresholds and synthetic stress tests.

Traffic-slicing patterns (practical examples)
- Orthogonal slices: route by user cohort attribute (new-user vs power-user), device, and geography. Ensure slices are orthogonal to experiment dimension to avoid confounding.
- Burst-aware sampling: when traffic volume spikes, cap absolute canary requests per minute to avoid overwhelming variant backends; convert excess to baseline.
- Cost-priority routing: route low-cost variants (quantized or smaller model) for non-critical cohorts; maintain parity for cohorts where quality is essential.

Privacy / legal checklist (quick)
- Ensure PII redaction pipeline runs before any sample is exported to human reviewers.
- If private-deployed customer traffic used for experiments, confirm contractual permission and KMS ownership.
- Maintain record of all canary allocations and samples for 90 days for audit.

Pre-flight rehearsals (recommended short script)
- 1) Run synthetic smoke: 5000 queries through routing path, check spans and model tags.
- 2) Dry-run metric comparing synthetic distribution to production baseline.
- 3) Manual review: 20 samples by product and 20 samples by applied-ml for content quality.
- 4) Load test: controlled burst to validate autoscaling and queueing behavior.

Experiment charter template (copyable)
- Experiment name: [short id]
- Owner: [name, email]
- Model/version: [vX.Y]
- Upstream change: [model weights / runtime / quantization / kernel change]
- Primary metric: [quantifiable metric + direction + threshold]
- Secondary metrics: [latency, error, cost, safety flag delta]
- Allocation plan: [0.5% → 1% → 2% → 5% → ...]
- Observation windows: [mins/hours/days]
- Abort conditions: [explicit cutoffs e.g., p95 > 2x baseline, safety flag rate > 3x baseline, customer SLA breach]
- Rollback plan: [immediate auto-rollback or manual?]
- Stakeholders: [list]

Open questions / low-priority ideas (parking lot)
- Can we add an automatic prompt-privacy redactor that runs inline before human sample exports? (infra + legal).
- Should we add cost-weighted canary scoring to bias routing during high-cost periods? (product + economics).
- Explore runbooks for multi-model fallback where one model provides fallback reranks (applied-ml + serving-runtime).

Immediate action items (owner: Ava)
- [ ] Add synthetic smoke harness to nightly jobs (JIRA: PROD-4532).
- [ ] Template the canary observation snapshot into the canary Slack alert (PR: github.com/.../87).
- [ ] Schedule rehearsal with SRE and Applied ML on 2025-07-25 (calendar invite).

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- Balance between human review and automated checks is messy for LLM features. For low-frequency high-impact cohorts, we should prefer more human review early.
- Keep thresholds conservative for early adopters on Dedicated/Private because rollback latency may be longer due to infra constraints.

References and existing artifacts:
- rollout-orchestration-overview (Confluence) — high-level architecture
- PROD-4532 — add synthetic harness
- PR #87 — Slack alert template for canary snapshots

If you're picking this up: please add any missing signals we need (user-correction-rate instrumentation + per-cohort cost attribution). Feel free to copy the observation template into your experiment's slack message and adapt thresholds for your funnel.
